title: JSRF durable review record
description: One acceptance-review transaction. Schema version 1, matching scripts/jsrf_review_records.py SCHEMA_VERSION and docs/packets/p0-review-records.md revision P0.2-interface-r14. A record is acceptance-eligible only when every required criterion is AGREED, every declared hash matches existing bytes, the verdict equals the text of the completed turn it names in the source session, and the reviewer's own completed turn carries an authoritative footer map agreeing with the record. LIMIT: this proves the record is SELF-CONSISTENT, not that the review happened -- a party who can author both the session log and the tracked source file satisfies every binding, because there is no trust anchor outside the files the record names.

schema_version.description: Must equal PROFILE... SCHEMA_VERSION in jsrf_review_records.py. An unknown version is INVALID, never a pass.

review_id.description: Stable identity of this review, used for the record filename.

packet_id.description: Must equal the required-criterion manifest's packet_id.

contract_sha256.description: Must equal the manifest's contract hash AND the contract file's actual bytes.

reviewed_files.description: Every file the review covers. A byte change to any of them invalidates the record under the post-review rule.

harness.description: Which source adapter produced the identity evidence.

parent_id.description: The session that spawned the reviewer. Read from the source, never transcribed.

child_id.description: The reviewer child. Ancestry must match the source's own header.

kind.description: Only turn_text is supported: the reviewer's own completed turn, written to a tracked file.

source_session.description: MANDATORY. The original harness log the turn was drawn from, so the validator can RE-OPEN it and verify ancestry, the completed turn and the route instead of trusting the record. Measured fail-open before this was required: `parent_id`, `child_id`, `turn_id`, `requested_model`, `requested_effort` and `harness` could all be set to arbitrary values at once -- including `parent_id=session-TOTALLY-DIFFERENT` -- and the record still returned acceptance-eligible, because only the PRESENCE of each key was checked. A record that omits this is INVALID.

turn_id.description: The selected COMPLETED turn. A turn whose turn/end reason is 'error' is refused.

verdict_text.description: AUTHORITY SCOPE: the single assistant message whose footer supplies the map. It must end, at its last non-empty line, with exactly one top-level REVIEW_CRITERIA_JSON: footer. It must also EQUAL the text of the completed turn named by `turn_id` in the source session: an independent review measured that binding `verdict_text` only to a tracked-file hash and to `contradiction_evidence` containment let a record declare a genuinely verified ancestry and an INVENTED verdict body -- and the verdict body carries the dispositions. Line endings and trailing whitespace are normalised; nothing else is.

contradiction_evidence.description: CONTRADICTION SCOPE, mandatory. The wider text the verdict was drawn from (normally the whole turn). It must CONTAIN verdict_text. Omitting it, or supplying one that does not contain the verdict, is INVALID -- measured, making it optional restored a fail-open in which a DISAGREED verdict in an earlier message was disowned by a footer quoted in a later one.

criteria.description: Must satisfy map EQUALITY with the required-criterion manifest, not a subset. An empty list fails.

disposition.description: UNKNOWN is deliberately NOT storable: a footer UNKNOWN is recorded as CANNOT VERIFY and stays pending.

evidence.description: Empty evidence is CANNOT VERIFY, never a pass. NOTE: no minItems here on purpose -- an empty list is a well-formed record with insufficient evidence, which is FAILED/pending (exit 1), not INVALID (exit 2). Enforcing minItems would report a malformed record where the amendment specifies an unverified criterion.

procedure.description: Empty or whitespace-only is CANNOT VERIFY (exit 1), not INVALID, so there is deliberately no minLength. NOTE: a nonempty check cannot distinguish a real command from plausible-sounding text; that limit is documented, not enforced.

observed_result.description: Empty is CANNOT VERIFY (exit 1), not INVALID, so there is deliberately no minLength.

delta.description: Optional. Present when the record was rebound after a post-review edit. A re-bind is NOT a re-review: it records the delta so the reviewer can confirm the change is confined to non-criterion text.

affected_criteria.description: Criteria the delta may affect. Empty only when the criterion-bearing text is measured unchanged.
